ai.headline: Meta launches Muse Spark 1.1; OpenAI releases GPT-5.6; Anthropic ships Claude Wrapped
ai.body: Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 targets coding performance improvements, with Zuckerberg signalling aggressive pricing against what he called 'very extreme' competitor costs. OpenAI simultaneously shipped GPT-5.6. Rapid concurrent model releases across all three frontier labs compress the competitive window for any single capability advantage.

ai.headline: ByteByteGo: Multi-agent deep research architecture — planner, sub-agents, synthesizer, citation agent
ai.body: ByteByteGo's breakdown of LLM deep-research pipelines describes a four-layer agentic architecture: query planner, specialised sub-agents with tool access (web, code execution), a synthesiser, and a citation agent. This maps closely to patterns emerging in production agentic systems and is relevant for anyone designing AI-augmented fraud or risk investigation workflows.

swe.headline: Docker internals: CLI → dockerd → containerd → runc → Linux namespaces/cgroups
swe.body: ByteByteGo maps the full container startup chain: Docker CLI sends an API call to dockerd, which delegates lifecycle management to containerd, which calls runc to create Linux namespaces and mount the OCI bundle. Isolation is purely kernel-level (namespaces, cgroups, network namespaces) — no guest OS or hypervisor. Useful mental model for debugging container security boundaries and IAM-adjacent workload isolation.

swe.headline: Keyset and cursor-based pagination outperform offset at scale — practical comparison of four strategies
swe.body: ByteByteGo compares offset, keyset, continuation-token, and time-based pagination: offset scans all skipped rows so deep pages degrade linearly, while keyset uses indexed lookups making page 1 and page 10,000 equivalent in cost. Continuation tokens (used by S3, YouTube) encapsulate cursor logic server-side but require stable query parameters across pages. Directly applicable to high-volume transaction/audit-log APIs in fintech.

mkt.headline: SK Hynix Nasdaq IPO: $1T memory chipmaker debuts with 7x oversubscription, +12.76% on day one
mkt.body: SK Hynix listed on Nasdaq seeking ~$28B to fund expansion including an Indiana fab, with preliminary orders oversubscribed 7x. Q1 2026 profits surged nearly 5x YoY driven by HBM demand from Nvidia; analysts expect the memory supply crunch to persist through at least 2027. The IPO is a direct read on AI infrastructure capex momentum and a benchmark for upcoming Anthropic and OpenAI listings.

mkt.headline: Netflix shares down 40% over 12 months; exploring live genre channels and third-party streaming bundles
mkt.body: Netflix TV viewership hit its lowest point since May 2025 (per Nielsen) despite being the #1 streamer by subscribers, prompting reported discussions about launching always-on genre channels and bundling rival platforms — mimicking Amazon and Apple. Ad revenue is projected to double to ~$3B in 2026, making live linear formats strategically attractive for incremental inventory.
